persona.name: Otieno
persona.background: Son of a Kenya Railways clerk; in 1995 he is 16 at a day secondary school. Music reaches him through KBC General Service in Swahili and the KBC English Service, Luo benga cassettes his father plays on Sundays, Congolese rumba at weddings and in Eastlands bars, ragga and US hits blasting from matatus, and the Sunday disco at a hall in town.

seeds.song: D.O. Misiani & Shirati Jazz - Benga Blast!
Shirati Jazz - Benga Beat
Papa Wemba - Yolele
Buju Banton - Champion
Remmy Ongala & Orchestre Super Matimila - Mambo Kwa Soksi
Marvin Gaye - What's Going On

KE1995A.wouldSay: Misiani, yes, my father's music, but which song is 'Benga Blast'? That is the name on a mzungu CD, not a song we sang. Buju Banton - now that is the matatu to Kencom.
missing: Princess Jully - Dunia Mbaya (early 1990s, year unsure)
KE1995A.fake: The two Kenyan seeds are Western export album titles (Benga Blast!, Benga Beat) rather than songs, and the rest is a world-music-shop selection with only one Kenyan artist, so it is not two-thirds local and the actual Kenyan radio and matatu sound of 1995 is missing.
suspect: D.O. Misiani & Shirati Jazz - Benga Blast! (album title, not a track)
Shirati Jazz - Benga Beat (compilation album title, not a track)

persona.name: Moussa
persona.town: Bamako (Médina Coura, near the railway station)
persona.background: Son of a railway mechanic for the Régie du chemin de fer; at 15 in 1975 he hears Radio Mali, sneaks in to hear the Rail Band at the Buffet Hôtel de la Gare, spends evenings at the grin with a transistor radio, goes to 'surprise-parties' with soul and Congolese 45s, and hears Guinean Syliphone records of Bembeya; Quran recitation at the mosque and on Friday radio.

seeds.song: Abdul Basit Abdul Samad - Surat Maryam
Bembeya Jazz National - Mami Wata
Babatunde Olatunji - Jin-Go-Lo-Ba

ML1975A.wouldSay: A Quran recitation to start a dance playlist? Then a song I don't know and American drums. Where is the Rail Band? Where is anything from Bamako?
missing: Bembeya Jazz National - Regard sur le passé (1969)
Franco & TPOK Jazz - Azda (1973, year unsure)
ML1975A.fake: There is not one Malian artist: an Egyptian Quran recitation, a Bembeya title I cannot place, and a 1959 Nigerian-American drum record that never reached Bamako.
suspect: Bembeya Jazz National - Mami Wata (title not found in Bembeya's known discography)
